_doc: THE OP VOCABULARY -- every primitive document op `op_apply` accepts, as data (node A3b, docs/AGENT_API.md section 4).
WHY THIS FILE EXISTS. A proposal (docs/AGENT_API.md) carries primitive ops, and until this file those ops were declared
nowhere but as two `match` statements (jas_dioxus/src/document/op_apply.rs `op_apply`, JasSwift/Sources/Document/
OpApply.swift `opApply`). A generated tool schema needs the vocabulary as data, so it is stated once, here.
CLASSES. `history` ops move the journal cursor or its boundaries (OP_LOG.md section 5) and are never journaled.
`selection` ops write the non-journaled selection channel; they are exactly each port's `is_selection_only_verb` set.
WHAT IS ASSERTED. scripts/check_op_vocabulary.py asserts that both ports' `op_apply` verb sets EQUAL the keys below and
that both ports' selection-only sets EQUAL the `selection` class. The MCP core's `propose` tool takes its `op` enum from
WHAT IS NOT DECLARED HERE, and there is nothing missing from this file for that reason: each op's ARGUMENTS. The arms
hand `op` to helpers that read keys elsewhere, so a static scan cannot enumerate them, and a hand-typed list would be
correct-not-verified. The arguments are the next slice of A3b.
